subject: Data lifecycle & de-identification RFI — Cascade Health
messages:
From: Ellen Price <ellen.price@cascadehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cascadehealth.com, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@cascadehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:10:00Z
Subject: RFI — data lifecycle, de-identification and retention (Cascade Health)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of Cascade Health's vendor review we need written responses to a short RFI focused on PHI handling: de-identification approaches, retention limits, access to raw PHI, and audit logging. Specifically:

1) Do you support both Safe Harbor and Expert Determination de-identification methods? If so, outline the processes and where they are applied.
2) What is your default retention period for: (a) raw request payloads that may contain PHI, (b) inference logs and traces, (c) aggregated telemetry?
3) Describe key management and separation of keys for customers who want BYOK.
4) Can customers request deletion of specific records and what is the SLA for deletion?
5) Provide sample audit log fields and retention options for logs.

We'd like responses in a PDF and any supporting attachments we can share with our security and procurement teams. Can you get this to us by COB tomorrow?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Price
Director, Vendor Risk
Cascade Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI — data lifecycle, de-identification and retention (Cascade Health)

Olga — draft below and attached. Key points:

- De-identification: We support both Safe Harbor (18 identifiers removal) and Expert Determination workflows. Safe Harbor is available as a self-service config for batch exports; Expert Determination is executed by our third-party statistics partner (summary report attached) and recommended when re-identification risk is non-trivial.

- Retention defaults (recommended):
  • Raw request payloads with PHI: 30 days by default; can be configured to 0 days (no persistent storage) for Dedicated/Private customers.
  • Inference logs & traces: 90 days default; option for 7/30/365 day tiers.
  • Aggregated telemetry: 2 years (aggregate-only, no PHI).

- BYOK & KMS: Customer-managed keys supported via KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). We maintain strict key separation for storage and ephemeral keys for inference; encryption-at-rest + envelope encryption.

- Deletion SLA: For account-scoped deletion requests we commit to logical deletion within 24 hours and irrecoverable removal from primary systems within 30 days; backup destruction subject to backup window but we document and notify.

- Audit logs: sample fields attached (timestamp, request_id, model, route, redaction_flag, requester_identity, action, source_ip, retention_tier). Can be exported to customer's SIEM or pushed to a customer-managed bucket.

I've attached: Redwood_Data_Lifecycle_Responses_20261201.pdf (one-page summary + appendix) and a sample audit CSV. Vivek — please review the BYOK wording and confirm the "ephemeral inference key" description matches runtime behavior.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Price <ellen.price@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@cascadehealth.com>, security@cascadehealth.com
Date: 2026-12-01T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI — data lifecycle, de-identification and retention (Cascade Health)

Hi Ellen,

Thanks for the RFI. Attached is a concise response packet and a BAA redline for review: Redwood_Data_Lifecycle_Responses_20261201.pdf and BAA_Redline_Cascade_20261201.docx. Highlights below:

- We support both Safe Harbor and Expert Determination; Safe Harbor for export and Expert Determination for high-risk datasets (we work with a third-party statistician).
- Default retention: raw payloads 30 days (configurable to 0), inference logs 90 days (tiered options), aggregated telemetry 2 years.
- BYOK: integrations with major KMS providers; patient data encryption uses envelope encryption with customer-managed root keys when requested.
- Deletion: logical deletion within 24 hours; irrecoverable removal within 30 days (backups documented).
- Audit logs: sample schema attached; we can stream logs to your SIEM or to a customer-managed bucket.

If you want to review specific BAA clauses, we've attached our proposed redline. Happy to set a short call with our security/engineering/legal folks tomorrow morning to run through any questions.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
Attachments: Redwood_Data_Lifecycle_Responses_20261201.pdf; BAA_Redline_Cascade_20261201.docx; audit-logging-sample.csv

From: Ellen Price <ellen.price@cascadehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cascadehealth.com, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@cascadehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:32:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI — small clarifications

Olga — thanks for the quick packet, very helpful. A couple of clarifications before we advance to procurement:

1) For Expert Determination: can you confirm whether the statistician provides a written report with k-anonymity / re-identification risk metrics that we can store? Is that part of the service or an add-on?
2) For customers choosing 0-day raw payload retention in Hosted mode — is there any transient access to plaintext beyond the single inference request? We need strong assurances about no persistent caches.
3) On deletion SLA: can you provide an example of the deletion workflow (who approves, audit evidence, and a sample notification that we could include in a SOW)?

If you can respond by EOD today we can share with our procurement team and get the SOW started.

Thanks — Ellen

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
